note:
, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN: the literature's earnings-announcement premium sits in the
announcement window itself (T-1 to T+1), not in the weeks before; pre-announcement drift is
weak and unstable across eras; and a run-up long is also a long on the market during reporting
season, which is why the excess is measured against SPY on the same dates. Claude expects the
run-up windows to read near zero and the event window to carry whatever premium exists.

verdict.reading: The raw run-up is survivorship and beta: today's 147-name universe beat SPY by +0.94% per 20 sessions whether or not a print was coming. Demeaned by each name's own drift in its era, the 20-session run-up is dead (+0.08, t 0.33) and the 10-session run-up is a thin residual (+0.34/wk, t 2.16) that vanishes in 2016-20 and does not clear the bar once the best week is dropped (t 1.94). The announcement window itself carries the premium (+0.60, t 3.64) and is a binary event the charter does not trade. The desk's current post-print window is the weakest of the four (-0.04). Measured 2026-09-17 on 6,442 announcements / 735 weeks; nothing registered, nothing traded.
